steps.name: 01_read_frame_a
steps.note: frame 56 of the brightfield channel, exactly as it comes off the recording. This is the only thing the estimator is ever shown.

steps.name: 02_read_frame_b
steps.note: frame 72, the other half of the comparison, 16 timepoints later.

steps.name: 03_prepared_a
steps.note: the 3 by 3 median the declared recipe asks for, on a copy. The recording itself is never written to; this frame exists only to be measured.

steps.name: 04_prepared_change_a
steps.note: what the median filter actually moved, and in which direction. Almost all of it is single-pixel noise; no structure is removed.

steps.name: 05_log_a
steps.note: log2(intensity + 1). The picture is unchanged - the logarithm changes the arithmetic, not the scene: a brightness change that multiplies every pixel becomes one number added to every pixel, which is what lets a single subtraction remove it.

steps.name: 06_log_b
steps.note: the same for the second frame.

steps.name: 07_valid_a
steps.note: which pixels are usable. With no intensity band declared for this recipe every finite pixel qualifies, so the mask is full - it is drawn because the engine still carries and consults it at every step.

steps.name: 08_gx_a
steps.note: how fast log intensity changes left-to-right at each pixel. The fit reads position out of these slopes: a pixel on a flat patch cannot say where it moved, a pixel on a slope can.

steps.name: 09_gy_a
steps.note: the same top-to-bottom.

steps.name: 10_gradient_magnitude_a
steps.note: |gx| + |gy|: total local structure. Bright where the frame has something to register on. Every LogPlane computes these three the moment it is built, whether or not the configured recipe goes on to read them - under this recipe the fit reads the second frame's, below, and not these.

steps.name: 11_gx_b
steps.note: the left-to-right slope of the second frame. This is the one the solve actually reads: the fit asks how far it must move the second frame for its slopes to explain the disagreement, so the Jacobian is built from the target frame's gradients, not the reference frame's.

steps.name: 12_gy_b
steps.note: the same top-to-bottom, and the other column of the Jacobian.

steps.name: 13_gradient_magnitude_b
steps.note: |gx| + |gy| for the second frame: where the fit can read a position from, and by contrast the flat interior where it cannot.

steps.name: 14_pyramid_a_L0
steps.note: level 0 of the first frame: 512 by 512, each step blurred with a 5-tap kernel and then halved. The coarse levels are where a large displacement is cheap to find; the fine ones are where it is made exact.

steps.name: 15_pyramid_a_L1
steps.note: level 1 of the first frame: 256 by 256, each step blurred with a 5-tap kernel and then halved. The coarse levels are where a large displacement is cheap to find; the fine ones are where it is made exact.

steps.name: 16_pyramid_a_L2
steps.note: level 2 of the first frame: 128 by 128, each step blurred with a 5-tap kernel and then halved. The coarse levels are where a large displacement is cheap to find; the fine ones are where it is made exact.

steps.name: 17_pyramid_a_L3
steps.note: level 3 of the first frame: 64 by 64, each step blurred with a 5-tap kernel and then halved. The coarse levels are where a large displacement is cheap to find; the fine ones are where it is made exact.

steps.name: 18_pyramid_b_L0
steps.note: level 0 of the second frame.

steps.name: 19_pyramid_b_L1
steps.note: level 1 of the second frame.

steps.name: 20_pyramid_b_L2
steps.note: level 2 of the second frame.

steps.name: 21_pyramid_b_L3
steps.note: level 3 of the second frame.

steps.name: 22_coarse_search_cost
steps.note: the cost of every whole-pixel displacement the engine tried at the coarsest level: one number per candidate position, brightest where the two frames disagree least. This is the only exhaustive search in the method; everything after it is a local step.

steps.name: 23_solve_L3i0_difference
steps.note: level 3, iteration 0: raw log difference between the two frames at the displacement this level started from, before the frame-wide gain is taken out

steps.name: 24_solve_L3i0_residual
steps.note: level 3, iteration 0: what is left after the one frame-wide gain number is removed - the field the fit is driven by

steps.name: 25_solve_L3i0_weight
steps.note: level 3, iteration 0: the Huber weight each pixel is given - 1 where it counts in full, less where it is bounded

steps.name: 57_residual_identity
steps.source: difference - gain, at the identity transform
steps.note: the disagreement between the two frames before anything is fitted, with the frame-wide gain already taken out. The structure left in it is the movement.

steps.name: 58_residual_fitted
steps.source: difference - gain, at the fitted transform
steps.note: the same field at the fitted displacement. It flattens because the frames now overlap - nothing has been brightened, sharpened or filled in.

steps.name: 59_pair_plan
steps.note: every comparison the engine will make, fixed before a single pixel is read: 1169 pairs over 240 frames at lags 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. One diagonal per lag. Because several routes connect any two timepoints, no single comparison can decide where a frame goes.

steps.name: 60_warp_input_bf_last
steps.note: the last brightfield frame before the transform is applied - five days after the first.

steps.name: 61_warp_output_bf_last
steps.note: the same frame after its own transform. The whole picture has moved by 3.77 across and 0.16 down, and the strip it vacated has no source pixel at all.

steps.name: 62_warp_vacated_bf_last
steps.note: exactly which pixels the warp left with nothing behind them. This is why a crop is needed: these are not dark pixels, they are absent ones.

steps.name: 63_warp_output_bioluminescence_last
steps.note: the identical transform applied to the Bioluminescence channel. The movement was measured on brightfield alone and then applied unchanged to every channel - the signal channels are never allowed to influence where they are put.

steps.name: 64_warp_output_rfp_last
steps.note: the identical transform applied to the RFP channel. The movement was measured on brightfield alone and then applied unchanged to every channel - the signal channels are never allowed to influence where they are put.

steps.name: 65_warp_output_gfp_last
steps.note: the identical transform applied to the GFP channel. The movement was measured on brightfield alone and then applied unchanged to every channel - the signal channels are never allowed to influence where they are put.

steps.name: 66_common_valid_field
steps.note: the field that holds a real source pixel at every one of the 240 timepoints, over the whole recording rather than this one frame: 0 columns off the left, 4 off the right, 1 rows off the top, 1 off the bottom.

steps.name: 67_cropped_bf_last
steps.note: the output: 508 by 510 of the original 512 by 512, every pixel of it real at every timepoint.
